episodes.176429: A cold front crossed central Pennsylvania during the afternoon of February 21, 2023, preceded by bands of gusty low-topped rain showers and thunderstorms, aided by steep lapse rates and appreciable deep-layer shear. Small (sub-severe) hail was also observed in some locations.
episodes.176853: A strong through moved through the region on the evening of February 20th to bring widespread Flash Flooding over Tutuila. There were multiple reports of homes being inundated from the flooding waters and caused delays to the Hawaiian Airlines flight to/from Honolulu. WSO Pago Pago received 4.41 inches of rain between 8:20 PM SST and 11:50 PM SST. A tipping bucket rain gauge in the village of Nuuuli recorded 1.99 inches of rain between 10:04 PM SST and 10:24 PM SST.
episodes.176855: A strong through moved through the region on the evening of February 20th over Tutuila. WSO Pago Pago observed cloud to ground lightning at times between 9 PM and 11 PM.
episodes.176860: A line of convective showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a passing cold front in Central New York. These storms became severe thanks to high shear being present on a cool February day. Strong winds knocked down trees and wires, mainly in Broome County. There were also some reports of 3/4 hail.
episodes.176861: A line of convective showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a passing cold front in Northeastern Pennsylvania. These storms became severe thanks to high shear being present on a cool February day. Strong winds knocked down trees and wires across the region. Some minor damage to personal property was also reported.
episodes.176879: A robust mid-level short wave with a surface cold front brought scattered severe weather to our region. Severe thunderstorms in NJ developed, aided by a high shear/low CAPE environment. One supercell spawned a tornado.
episodes.176948: Heavy rainfall elevated streams across the island with efficient runoff due to high soil moisture content and locally intense rainfall rates.
episodes.176956: Soils on the windward side of the Big Island, near Hilo, were nearly saturated and fatigued due previous rounds of heavy rainfall that occurred over the past several days, which created a landslide near Honomu.
episodes.176957: An extended period of enhanced rainfall with embedded locally heavy rainfall rates overwhelmed a few local roads on Pearl City Peninsula.
episodes.177033: Minor flooding occurred along sections of the Ohio River. The flooding was due to a series of frontal passages that brought showers and thunderstorms on ground that was already very moist. The widespread heavy rain event on the 16th was the primary reason for this minor flooding event on the Ohio River.
episodes.178054: A powerful and cold storm system with heavy snow and gusty winds brought blizzard conditions. Snow amounts of 2 to near 5 feet were reported in the mountains. Significant snow fell down into the northern Sacramento Valley, with 3 to 8 inches of accumulation impacting travel. Many schools were closed or had delays. Wind gusts of 40-60 mph were recorded across the area, with gusts locally higher in the high elevations of the northern Sierra. The winds and low snow combined to cause dangerous travel conditions numerous road closures, including a closure of Interstate 5 north of Fawndale, on US Highway 50 and an extended closure of Interstate 80 across the Sierra.

After the Hawaiian Airlines flight landed at the Pago Pago International Airport from Honolulu, Hawaii, passengers remained onboard for two hours before being able to deplane. Due to heavy rainfall and lightning in the area, the captain decided to keep the passengers onboard due to safety reasons. The outbound flight was delayed through late in the afternoon on the 21st.

Sporadic minor tree damage was observed west of Interstate 295. A continuous path of tree damage was observed near Lawrence Station Road, particularly in a housing development along Fountayne Lane. Additional tree damage and damage to roofing occurred in a housing development at Lawrence Square. Estimated maximum wind speeds in this area were 105-115 MPH. In a straight line from this damage, there was roofing damage at a residence and a commercial building as well as additional tree damage along Quaker Bridge Road. Tree damage continued at a park across the street and through the 2nd and 11th holes at the adjacent golf course. Additional sporadic tree damage occurred in residential areas east of the golf course in West Windsor Township. The last tree damage was observed near the intersection of Old Trenton Road and Village Road.

More than 800 PG&E customers in the downtown area of Chico were without power on the afternoon of 2/21. The outage was between Main Street and Orange Street and between W. 1st Street and W. 7th Street. Some traffic lights were reported out. Winds at Chico Airport were sustained at 31 mph with gusts to 49.5 mph.
